stem.text: Consider the differential equation \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - 6 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 42 \sin{\left(x \right)} \). Decide whether it can be solved by separation of variables. If it can, write it with every factor involving y on the side of dy and every factor involving x on the side of dx; if it cannot, say so.

worked_solution.text: The two terms share the factor \( - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)} \), so \( \frac{dy}{dx} = - 6 y \sin{\left(x \right)} - 42 \sin{\left(x \right)} = - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)}\left(y + 7\right) \), a function of x times a function of y.
worked_solution.rule_named: right side factored into a function of x times a function of y

worked_solution.text: Divide by \( y + 7 \) and multiply by dx: \( \frac{dy}{y + 7} = - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx \).

options.label: \( \frac{dy}{y} = \left(- 42 \sin{\left(x \right)} - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)}\right)dx \)
options.derivation: only the first term divided by y, as though the sum split term by term

options.label: \( \left(y + 7\right)dy = - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)}\,dx \)
options.derivation: the factor y + 7 multiplied onto the dy side instead of divided

options.label: \( dy = - 6 \sin{\left(x \right)}\left(y + 7\right)\,dx \)
options.derivation: dx moved across with y still on the side of dx, so nothing was separated
